status_definition: Complete means that all preregistered jobs and integrity gates finished; it is not a scientific acceptance verdict.
decision: Within this fixed five-seed panel, p=1 training degraded mean p=0.05 performance less than direct p=0.05 standard-rate training, but did not outperform the pre-continuation source checkpoint, p=0.30 standard-rate training, either preregistered quarter-rate comparator, or the p=0 continuation. The contrast identifies the complete configured training-probability intervention, not exposure count alone, and does not support a monotonic benefit from increasing training probability to 1.

evidence_scope.prospective: The p=0 and p=1 standard-rate branches, five seeds each, were fixed before launch and newly trained.
evidence_scope.retrospective: The p=0.05 and p=0.30 standard- and quarter-rate policies were reused from the pinned prior experiment. The p=0.30-to-p=0.05 transfer clue was known before this launch.
evidence_scope.cross_probability_evaluation: Every number in the exact mode matrices is a finite-panel formula evaluation of deterministic normal-kernel paths, not a new stochastic rollout.
evidence_scope.independent_unit: learner seed; all five seed values are retained and no significance claim is made.

supported: Relative to the degraded p=0.05 standard-rate branch, both p=0.30 and p=1 training transferred better to p=0.05 evaluation within this fixed budget.
Increasing training probability from 0.30 to 1 did not improve mean p=0.05 return at the standard rate; p=1 was lower by 0.00423.
The p=1 policy nearly eliminated risky starts but lost 2.5 percentage points of normal-kernel success and remained below the untrained source by 0.00155 return at p=0.05.
The retrospective p=0.30 quarter-rate condition had the highest tested p=0.05 mean return, 0.88854, while preserving 100% normal-kernel success.
interpretation.heterogeneity: The p=1-minus-direct-p=0.05 contrast was positive in four seeds but strongly negative in seed 35, whose p=1 final policy also had only 87.5% normal-kernel success. Every negative p=1 mean contrast reverses when seed 35 is omitted, so the condition ranking is descriptive and unstable.
interpretation.training_harm: The five p=1 jobs lost 15,045 grain during collection, versus 6,789 for prior p=0.30 standard-rate training and 1,279 for prior direct p=0.05 standard-rate training. These totals reflect different event probabilities and training objectives, not event-count-only causal effects.
not_claimed: that p=0.30 is globally optimal or that probabilities between tested points are ordered
that frequent training helps beyond preventing degradation in the direct standard-rate branch
that event count alone caused the transfer result
that five learner seeds establish statistical significance
that the analytic matrix is an independent stochastic rollout
that lower risk exposure alone constitutes successful adaptation

validation.focused_tests: 20 related CPU tests passed with one dependency deprecation warning.
validation.decimal_recomputation: All 30 final policies, 32 starts, and four evaluation probabilities were recomputed with 80-digit Decimal arithmetic from 70 directly hashed input files. Maximum difference from the binary64 result was 2.8079904770065535e-16.
validation.post_training_aggregation_fix: The first aggregation attempt stopped before writing a result because it required exact source/new config key equality. The aggregation source was then changed to allow only the preregistered inventory_overwrite_probability key absent from the fixed source config; all non-intervention fields remained equality-checked. Execution-time and aggregation-time source hashes are recorded separately.
validation.shared_implementation_limit: The independent arithmetic audit does not independently validate simulator dynamics, checkpoint semantics, or the causal interpretation.
